title: Chain of Custody & SIEM Pipeline Playbook
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines a repeatable chain-of-custody process for security incidents that require evidence collection, preservation, and export to the SIEM and legal teams. Goal: ensure evidentiary integrity, minimize investigation latency, and automate exports while preserving access controls.

Scope:
- Applies to incidents where artifacts (core dumps, disk images, logs, packet captures, snapshots) are material to an investigation or regulatory audit.
- Excludes low-severity alerts (Triage-only, auto-closed) unless escalated.

Key principles:
- Provenance: every artifact must have an originating request id, collector id, timestamp, and hash (SHA256) stored in the evidence ledger.
- Least privilege: access to evidence is governed by RBAC v2 roles (see Roles section) and timebound sessions.
- Immutable packaging: evidence is packaged with a manifest and signed checksum before transfer to long-term storage.
- Automation-first: leverage SIEM ingestion, signed upload APIs, and an evidence broker service to reduce manual steps.

Roles and RBAC v2 mapping:
- ir-collector (role): can create artifacts, upload to temporary evidence bucket, add entries to evidence ledger.
- ir-analyst (role): can read evidence in temp bucket, create investigation notes, request exports.
- ir-legal (role): can request sealed exports to legal-retention storage; requires dual-approval.
- infra-auditor (role): read-only access to evidence ledger and audit log schema; cannot access raw artifacts.
- escalation-policy: temporary elevation (timeboxed) implemented via vault-issued short-lived credentials; all elevations recorded in audit logs.

Evidence ledger schema (minimal fields):
- evidence_id: unique uuid
- collector_id
- source_node
- artifact_type
- filename
- sha256
- size_bytes
- collected_at (ISO8601)
- uploaded_to_bucket
- access_policy_version
- retention_until
- linked_ticket (JIRA/Linear)
Note: ledger is stored in encrypted DB; schema also emits structured audit events to SIEM per the 'audit_event_type' mapping below.

Audit event mapping to SIEM:
- EVIDENCE_CREATED -> siem.event_type = "evidence.create", fields: evidence_id, collector_id, source_ip, sha256, size_bytes, linked_ticket
- EVIDENCE_ACCESSED -> siem.event_type = "evidence.access", fields: evidence_id, accessor, reason, access_method, ttl_expiry
- EVIDENCE_EXPORTED -> siem.event_type = "evidence.export", fields: evidence_id, export_target, approved_by, approval_ids
- EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH -> siem.event_type = "evidence.integrity_fail", fields: evidence_id, expected_sha256, observed_sha256, comparator_id
- RBAC_ELEVATION -> siem.event_type = "rbac.elevate", fields: principal, role, duration_seconds, issued_by

Automation pipeline (high-level):
1) Trigger: IR triage marks incident as "requires-evidence" -> triggers collector job with parameters.
2) Collector agents (sha1: collector v2.3) perform targeted artifact collection, compute sha256, and POST artifact to evidence broker API with metadata.
3) Evidence broker stores artifact in temp encrypted bucket (s3://ri-evidence-temp/<evidence_id>/) and writes ledger entry.
4) SIEM-log forwarder picks up 'EVIDENCE_CREATED' events and correlates with the incident id; alerts if high-volume collections from single host.
5) Analyst reviews in temp bucket, requests sealed export; approval workflow via Linear/JIRA ticket and dual-approval endpoint.
6) On approval, broker re-packages artifact into sealed container (tar + manifest + signature), uploads to long-term sealed bucket (s3://ri-evidence-sealed/) and emits EVIDENCE_EXPORTED.

Minimal manual checklist (for on-call):
- Mark incident with 'evidence-required' label and add linked ticket.
- Run collector via /tools/collector/run with incident id and target host(s).
- Verify ledger entry created and SHA256 matches local output: `sha256sum file`.
- If mismatch, note comparator id in ledger and escalate to forensics.
- For sealed export, obtain dual approvals and record approval ids; do not export without approvals.
- Notify legal@redwood.com if the evidence includes PII or customer data.

Packaging & verification example (commands):
- Collector computes: `sha256sum /tmp/core.dump > /tmp/core.dump.sha256`
- Upload: `curl -X POST -F file=@/tmp/core.dump https://evidence-broker.internal/api/v1/upload?incident=IR-1021`
- Verify ledger: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://evidence-ledger.internal/v1/evidence/uuid`
- Seal (on approval): `tar -czf evidence-<id>.tar.gz file; openssl dgst -sha256 -sign /keys/evidence-signing.pem -out evidence.sig evidence-<id>.tar.gz`

Retention and legal hold:
- Default retention for sealed evidence: 7 years for legal, 1 year for non-legal; retention_until stored in ledger.
- Legal hold overrides retention and requires legal team sign-off to delete.

Post-incident export and SIEM hygiene:
- After incident closure, run 'siem:annotate-incident' to link evidence events to postmortem.
- Archive temp buckets monthly; ensure garbage collection only deletes objects with retention_until < now and no active holds.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact schema versioning strategy for ledger and SIEM mapping (proposal: semver-like v1.0, v1.1 for non-breaking).
- Add automation test harness that simulates collector -> broker -> SIEM with replayable fixtures.
- Harden collector auth for air-gapped/private deployments.

Quick contacts & resources:
- Slack channel: #sec-incident-response
- Pager: sec-oncall@pagerduty (primary)
- Legal oncall: legal-oncall@redwood.com
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-SEC-CHAIN-02 (draft)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/314

Notes to self:
- Consider adding HSM-signed manifests for regulatory-sensitive regions.
- Explore direct SIEM bulk-export endpoint to avoid duplication of events.

End of playbook (working doc).
